```{r, include=FALSE}
task <- "tpaired5"

```

Question
========
In a study on depression, symptoms are measured on the 
Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS, from 0 to 60, 
with higher scores meaning more severe depression symptoms, 
reliability of measurement at 0.8) before and after the intervention. 
The new therapy is considered promising if a relevant reduction 
of more than $\mu_0 = `r mu_0`$ units is reached. 
The expected benefit of the new therapy is $\mu_D = `r mu_D`$ units. 
The standard deviation at $T0$ is `r s_t0`. 

Calculate the necessary sample size to reach a power of 90% ($\alpha=.05$ one-tailed).

```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The sample size calculation for a paired $t$-test involves calculating 
the standard deviation of the change score. 
For a power of 90% and a reliability of measurement at 0.8, 
this is given by $s_D = 0.63 \cdot s_{T0}$.

Next, we calculate the standardized effect size, given by $d = \dfrac{\mu_D - \mu_0}{s_D}$.

The sample size formula is then given by $N≈\dfrac{9}{d^2}$. Note to always round up this number!



```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
